slots.title: China PMI 49.8 beats 49.6 forecast
slots.body:
China’s August manufacturing PMI: 49.8.

Economists polled by Reuters had expected 49.6.

A reading below 50 means factory activity is still contracting — just not as sharply as feared.

The print landed as Asian indexes were already reacting to tighter U.S. rate expectations after Fed commentary at Jackson Hole.

slots.title: US cash session recap — Aug. 30, 2026
slots.body:
The Russell 2000 fell 1.4% to 2,972.37, the largest percentage decline among the major U.S. equity indexes in the session, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was nearly flat at 53,559.99 (down 0.0%).

The S&P 500 slipped 0.2% to 7,711.76 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.5% to 26,402.42, so the growth-heavy benchmark bore more of the session’s weakness than the large-cap blue-chip average.

NVIDIA was among the most active symbols by volume, closing down 4.6% at $217.55 on 194.8 million shares, after a prior session that had seen a sharp upward repricing.

Amazon.com finished up 4.0% at $266.43 with 49.5 million shares traded, making it one of the strongest megacap performers on a red index day.

Salesforce rose 1.6% to $256.00, Alphabet Class A gained 1.7% to $346.59, Netflix added 2.4% to $81.72, and Mastercard ticked up 0.6% to $595.30.

Financial megacaps also closed higher: Bank of America up 1.9% to $62.32 and JPMorgan Chase up 1.0% to $357.62.

On the weak side among large liquid names, ASML lost 2.2% to $1,696.16, Tesla fell 1.7% to $348.75, and Oracle slipped 0.8% to $150.72.

Elastic N.V. stood out in the liquid gainers screen, up 19.3% to $99.91; PG&E closed down 7.5% at $16.60 among actives.

No U.S. economic releases were listed in the session calendar payload for this close bundle.

Treasury snapshot dated 2026-08-28 showed the 10-year yield at 4.7% and the 2s10s spread at 0.39 percentage points.

The CBOE Volatility Index edged down 0.6% to 14.43.

Gold futures fell 1.2% to $4,476.00; the U.S. dollar proxy (UUP) rose 0.6% to $28.18; Brent crude rose 2.3% to $90.14; Bitcoin USD was up 0.1% at $77,772.62.

Overseas indexes in the bundle included the Nikkei 225 down 1.6% at 65,361.60, the Hang Seng down 0.6% at 25,421.00, and the FTSE 100 up 0.3% at 10,824.26.

Headlines in the feed tied oil to supply concerns after U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island, with Brent back above $90 in that reporting, while separate coverage linked Asian equity weakness and chip stocks to firmer U.S. rate-hike expectations after Fed commentary.

slots.title: JOLTs 7.39M estimate Monday at 2 p.m.
slots.body:
Monday, Sept. 1, at 2:00 p.m.
ET: two U.S. labor and factory prints land back to back.

JOLTs job openings for July carry a 7.39M estimate; the prior reading was 7.36M.

That series tracks how many jobs are open nationwide—useful for seeing whether hiring demand is still broad.

Same release window: ISM Manufacturing PMI for August is estimated at 55.3, down from 55.6.

Readings above 50 mean more factories reporting expansion than contraction.

ISM Manufacturing employment for August is estimated at 52.5; prior was 52.8.

Week window: Aug. 31–Sept. 4.

What do you watch first on Monday—openings or the factory PMI?
